notes: Vermont requires 'reasonable opportunities' to eat and use toilet facilities (DOL tables); no fixed duration, not encoded.
Vermont minimum wage applies to employers of 2+ employees.
No state meal-period requirement for adults in the DOL table; federal law does not require one.
No state paid rest-period requirement in the DOL table; federal law does not require one.
No state daily overtime listed in the DOL table.
Drafted from US DOL WHD state tables (confidence=medium) on 2026-11-06; upgrade to primary sources pending.
minimum_wage.effective is the DOL table date (2026-11-05), not the statutory effective date.
Minors (VT DOL WH-30; statutes site is JS-only): 16-17 limits (9 h/day, 50 h/week) apply only in manufacturing or mechanical establishments — not retail, not encoded. Extra param key max_days_week.

rules.summary: In school weeks, 14- and 15-year-olds may work at most 3 hours on a school day, 8 on a non-school day, 18 hours and 6 days a week, 7 a.m.-7 p.m. (9 p.m. June 1-Labor Day).

citation.title: Vermont Dept. of Labor WH-30 — Information for Employers, Child Labor Law (time and hour restrictions)
citation.excerpt: More than three hours per day, on school days. 4. More than eight hours per day, on non-school days. 5. More than 18 hours per week, in school weeks.

rules.summary: In non-school weeks, 14- and 15-year-olds may work at most 8 hours a day, 40 hours and 6 days a week, 7 a.m.-7 p.m. (9 p.m. June 1-Labor Day).

citation.title: Vermont Dept. of Labor WH-30 — Information for Employers, Child Labor Law (time and hour restrictions)
citation.excerpt: 6. More than 40 hours per week, in non-school weeks. 7. More than six days in a week. ... Before 7 AM or after 7 PM. (after 9:00 p.m. between June 1st and Labor Day)
